subject: ALPHACORP: sudden concurrency spike affecting checkout paths - standby coordination
messages:
From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@alphacorp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-eng@alphacorp.com
Date: 2026-10-11 08:12:42 -0400
Subject: Re: sudden spike - checkout 5xx + latency

Evelyn —

We started seeing a sustained jump in 5xx (+8%) and median p95 latency up ~420ms across checkout inference calls starting ~07:55 ET. Error rates are concentrated on the model route used for our personalized promo flow (route: /generate/promo). Throughput (tokens/sec) has dropped by ~35% while request concurrency is +60%. This is causing checkout timeouts and (~8%) failed transactions on our side.

Attached is a short log snippet and three sample traces for the timeframe (07:50-08:05). The impact is material for our morning batch — executives are pinging. Can you confirm whether this is on your side (serving layer) or if something in our traffic pattern could have caused it?

We need an immediate point-of-contact and a plan for mitigation; can you stand up a short war-room for 9:00 ET?

Thanks,
Simon
S. Lewis
Head of Platform Reliability, AlphaCorp

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-11 09:01:37 -0400
Subject: Re: sudden spike - checkout 5xx + latency

Folks — triage notes (initial):

- Observable: abrupt increase in queuing time on the model shards serving /generate/promo, coinciding with a higher-than-usual short-lived fanout of subrequests triggered by the new client-side caching layer alpha feature. That led to KV cache churn and higher GC pauses in the serving process.
- Impact: KV cache misses caused repeated prefix re-computation increasing per-request tokens and pushing requests into the tail of the scheduler. Backlog then caused the autoscaler to trigger a small scale-up which briefly increased cold-start latency and CPU contention.

Immediate actions taken (08:45-09:00 ET):
- Applied a soft throttle on promo route (limit moved to 60 rps from observed peak of 125 rps) — this reduced queue depth by ~55%.
- Deployed a targeted fallback route to the quantized-v2 model for non-personalized requests to reduce per-token cost and latency for high-concurrency bursts.
- Pinning: marked several hot shards to prefer warm instances (reduced cold starts).

Next steps for the war-room:
- Validate that alpha feature change is the trigger (Simon to confirm if the rollout correlated with 07:50 ET).
- If confirmed, propose throttling rollout rate on your side + gradual increase of dedicated capacity for promo route as a durable fix.
- Post-call: joint postmortem with timeline, RCA, and rate-limiting/SDK guardrails to prevent recurrence.

I've attached short sample traces and our checklist to the incident doc.

-David
David Kim
Head of Runtime Ops
Redwood Inference
